title: Searching and Sorting
summary: Linear and binary search with their invariants and the overflow-safe midpoint, the simple sorts (selection and insertion) and why they are O(n²), divide and conquer with merge sort and quicksort, stability, choosing a pivot, and what Java's own sorts use.

cards.q: Why is binary search O(log n)?
cards.a:
Each comparison halves the range that can still contain the target

Halving the range each step means a range of n items is down to one after about log₂ n comparisons.

cards.q: Merge sort is stable. What does that mean, and what in the merge makes it so?
cards.a:
Equal items keep their original order; taking from the left half when `a[i] <= a[j]` does that

On a tie the merge takes the item from the left half, which came first in the original. With `<` instead of `<=` equal items could swap places.

cards.q: Which sort is O(n log n) even in the worst case?
cards.a:
Merge sort

Merge sort always splits evenly; quicksort can degrade to O(n²) with bad pivots.
